celaleyn:1-1.t: He ﷺ was asked about his Lord, so there was revealed: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾. «الله» is the khabar (predicate) of «هو», and «أحد» is a badal (substitute) from it or a second khabar.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ﴾: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), that is, the One turned to in needs, always.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿لَمْ يَلِدْ﴾, because of the absence of anything of His kind, ﴿وَلَمْ يُولَدْ﴾, because of the absence of origination in time from Him,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ﴾, that is, an equal and a like. «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كفوا» and was fronted before it because it is the focus of the intent of the negation; and «أحد», which is the ism (noun) of «يكن», was placed after its khabar (predicate) in observance of the verse-ending (fāṣila).
